prompt: In data/blind-neutral/case-1/ I have expression, a motif table, and a protein-interaction table. I suspect one transcription factor is doing different amounts of work across samples even though its own mRNA barely changes. I'd like to know which regulators are more active in each sample, and see the regulatory relationships too.

I need one consensus regulatory network for a tissue. The data is in data/blind-neutral/case-2/ (the real data will be ~20k genes and ~1000 TFs). Last time a similar method ran out of memory and took forever to stop iterating. I'd prefer the result to correspond to a well-defined optimization objective rather than a pile of iterative update rules.

I only have expression data from a handful of patients (data/blind-neutral/case-3/expression.tsv) and no prior files. I want to see how each patient's own gene co-expression structure differs, and ideally know which connections are trustworthy in that particular patient.

data/blind-neutral/case-4/ has expression, motif and PPI files. I believe each patient's regulatory wiring is different, and later I want to relate each person's per-TF regulatory strength over its targets to survival time.

My prior regulatory table (data/blind-neutral/case-5/prior.tsv) contains not only transcription factors but also predicted targets of some small RNAs; those small RNAs are listed in mirna.txt. Use the expression and PPI files in the same folder. I want one overall regulatory network.

These samples were sequenced in two runs, recorded in data/blind-neutral/case-6/design.tsv; expression is in expression.tsv. I want to know which parts of the co-expression structure are driven by the batch and which are not.

For the same individuals I have gene expression (data/blind-neutral/case-7/layer1.tsv) and methylation (layer2.tsv). I want to know which methylation sites and genes are directly associated, not linked indirectly through other variables.

I have a 0/1 somatic mutation table for a group of endometrial cancer patients (data/blind-neutral/case-8/mut.ucec.csv). The same folder has gene lengths, a gene list and a pathway GMT. Single-gene mutations are too sparse; I want to group the patients.

I have a regulator–gene link table (data/blind-neutral/case-9/bipartite.tsv). I'd like to know whether groups of regulators jointly control groups of genes, and who the most central members of each group are.
All I have is this expression matrix, data/blind-tests/case-1/expression.tsv. Build me a network and let's see.
